sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

This application is preferred under Section 439(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure by the applicant - original complainant for cancellation of bail granted to the original accused by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.20, City Sessions Court, Ahmedabad vide order dated 01.05.2019 passed in Criminal Misc. Application No. 2910 of 2019 for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 420 etc of the Indian Penal Code in connection with the offence registered being C.R.
No.I - 14 of 2019 before Navrangpura Police Station, Ahmedabad.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Ms. Namrata Chauhan, learned advocate for the applicant and Ms. Maithili Mehta, learned APP for the respondent - State of Gujarat.

sentences.text: Ms.Chauhan, learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that while enlarging the accused on bail, the accused has committed the breach of condition imposed by the Trial Court.

She has submitted that the accused has not repaid the amount of loss occurred to the applicant company and even the Trial Court has not imposed the condition to repay the amount of loss occurred to the company.
She has submitted that the impugned order is ex facie illegal and arbitrary and that the same is passed without appreciating the facts and circumstances of the case.

She has, therefore,
urged before the Court that the application may be allowed and the bail granted to the accused may be cancelled.

In support of her submission, Ms.Chauhan, learned advocate has relied upon the decision of the Delhi High Court in the case of Trinity Global enterprises Limited VS. Raj Hiremath and another reported in 2012 SCC Online Del 3298.
4.

entities.text: Trinity Global enterprises Limited VS. Raj Hiremath and another reported in 2012 SCC Online Del 3298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ms.Mehta, learned Additional Public Prosecutor has submitted that after releasing the accused on bail there was no untoward or overwhelming circumstance reported against him and there was no breach of any condition reported against the accused.
Further she submitted that the trial is commenced and it is at the stage of recording of the evidence of the witnesses.
In view of the aforesaid facts, she has submitted that the Court may pass appropriate orders.

5. In the case of Trinity Global Enterprises (supra), the Delhi NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19825/2019 ORDER DATED: 19/08/2023 undefined High Court has considered the submissions and facts and has not imposed any condition with regard to repayment of the amount of loss occurred to the applicant.
In the said case, the observation made in paragraph no.26 by the Delhi High Court is in respect of that particular case, which is not similar to the present one.

It appears that it is not established by the applicant that the loss occurred to the company is at the behest of the accused and for that the company has not filed any civil proceedings for recovery of the amount and even the applicant has not produced any material to the effect that the accused is liable to repay the amount.
6. I have perused the FIR and the impugned order passed by the Trial Court in the application for regular bail.
I have considered the submissions canvassed by learned advocates appearing on behalf of both the sides and the averments made in the application.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the opinion that the Trial Court has rightly exercised its power under Section 438 of the Code.

7. Considering the facts of the present case, it appears that the main grievance of the present applicant is that while enlarging the accused on bail, the Trial Court has not imposed the condition of repayment of the amount of loss occurred to the applicant.
It is relevant to note that this is not the case of recovery proceedings and the applicant has not filed civil proceedings with regard to recovery of the amount.

The decision NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19825/2019 ORDER DATED:
19/08/2023 undefined relied upon by the learned advocate for the applicant is not applicable to the facts of the present case.

Normally in usual circumstance, the Court cannot interfere with the order passed by the Trial Court except in the case of any overwhelming circumstance or any breach of condition or any other special circumstance shown by the applicant.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and the case laws, I am of the opinion that in the present case, when the respondent original accused has been released on bail and has not committed any breach of conditions imposed by the Court and when there is no overwhelming circumstances, there is no reason to exercise power under Section 439(2) of the Code and cancel the bail granted in favour of the respondent - original accused.
Now, the trial is commenced and it is at the stage of recording of the evidence of the witnesses.
9. With aforesaid observations, present application deserves to be dismissed and accordingly it is dismissed.
The order passed by the Trial Court is hereby confirmed.
